selectors.name: Default correlation of two firms
selectors.what: Default correlation of two firms from their default probabilities and the joint default probability: rho12 = (pi12 - pi1 x pi2) / (sqrt(pi1(1 - pi1)) x sqrt(pi2(1 - pi2))).
selectors.theory: Defaults are Bernoulli variables; the covariance is pi12 - pi1 x pi2; independence gives pi12 = pi1 x pi2 and zero correlation; the larger the excess of pi12 over pi1 x pi2, the higher the correlation; one-year default correlations are small (about 0.05) but matter because PDs are small.

selectors.name: Joint probability of default, direct calculation
selectors.what: Joint default probability rebuilt from a given default correlation: pi12 = rho12 x sqrt(pi1(1 - pi1)) x sqrt(pi2(1 - pi2)) + pi1 x pi2. Includes the related outcomes: P(neither) = 1 - pi1 - pi2 + pi12, P(at least one) = pi1 + pi2 - pi12, P(exactly one) = pi1 + pi2 - 2 x pi12.
selectors.theory: pi12 is a primitive that cannot be computed from pi1 and pi2 unless defaults are independent; even a small correlation multiplies the joint probability many times over the independent value (Example 11.1: 5% correlation gives nearly 10 times the independent joint PD).

selectors.name: Default correlation, unequal default probabilities
selectors.what: Default correlation of two credits with different PDs (for example 0.25% and 1.25%, or high-yield PDs), where each standard deviation is sqrt(pi_i(1 - pi_i)) and the two terms differ.
selectors.theory: The denominator uses sqrt(pi_i(1 - pi_i)), not sqrt(pi_i); the gap matters most for high PDs; with unequal PDs the two standard deviations are not the same and cannot be collapsed to pi(1 - pi).

selectors.name: Gaussian copula and implied correlation
selectors.what: Joint default probability of two names from the bivariate normal, Q(t1 <= t, t2 <= t) = M2(N^-1(Q1(t)), N^-1(Q2(t)); rho), or the conditional PD in the one-factor Gaussian copula, Q(T|F) = N((N^-1[Q(T)] - a x F) / sqrt(1 - a^2)); and the implied (tranche) correlation backed out of a tranche price.
selectors.theory: A copula joins marginal distributions into a joint one; times to default are mapped percentile to percentile to standard normals, which are assumed multivariate normal (the transformed variables are normal, not the default times); the copula correlation is often proxied by equity return correlation. Implied correlation is the copula correlation that makes the modelled tranche value equal the market price: risk-neutral, market-based, varying by tranche (correlation skew), not a historical estimate.

selectors.name: Trap: omitting the pi1 x pi2 term
selectors.what: The correlation numerator is taken as the joint default probability without subtracting pi1 x pi2 (overstating the correlation), or pi12 is rebuilt without adding pi1 x pi2 back (understating it); the distractor option is the answer that drops the term.

selectors.name: Conditional default probability, common factor
selectors.what: Default probability of a firm given the common factor m in the single-factor model: p(m) = Phi((k_i - beta_i x m) / sqrt(1 - beta_i^2)) with k_i = Phi^-1(pi_i); for example beta = 0.4, pi = 1%, m = -1 gives 1.78%.
selectors.theory: Given the factor, defaults are independent; the conditional mean of the asset return is beta_i x m and the conditional standard deviation sqrt(1 - beta_i^2); the conditional PD differs from pi_i unless m = 0 or beta_i = 0; in a downturn (m < 0) a higher beta means a higher conditional PD; asset correlation is beta_i x beta_j and is far larger than default correlation.

selectors.name: Impacts table for tranches
selectors.what: LO 40.i: how a rise in default probability or in default correlation moves the risk and value of the equity, mezzanine and senior tranches of a securitization (Vardeez: remember the impacts via the table).
